quotes.text: But a clan whose stones showed many empty baskets found the river turning cold toward them.
*Never be the first to dim. Answer the hand, forgive the fog, and keep the ring unbroken.*
Tessaly carved the sixth line:
"The stones remember what the mist conceals. Every crossing teaches the valley who can be trusted.
The young clansman frowned. "Why reward them so richly? You gain less."
"Why give back so much? The mist hides your hand. No one would know."
she sent back more than half, so the brave sender would leave richer than he came
One thin basket is weather, not character.
His granddaughter asked, "What if the basket truly was lighter?"

note: Ages of the Misted Valley; reputation stones; one line carved per age; the cold river only for many empty baskets.

quotes.text: withdraw only from those who take again and again.

In the sixth season, Tamsa turned again, and Kelu woke downstream.
The elders teach: your deeds travel ahead of you.

Had the stranger been greedy, or had the fog swallowed the grain?
He floated back more than half, so the stranger would reach home richer for trusting.
Do not pass one stranger's hollowness to the next.
Why not keep your grain just once and see?

note: Kelu reads the reputation stone each season; refuses cousin's and bitterness' urgings to repay losses on innocent strangers.

quotes.text: They turned their light away only from those who drank again and again.
His lantern whispered, "Less came than before. Answer less in turn."
when trust arrives weary, honor it more, not less.
On the hill of dusk, the seventh season turned.
Oru gave each flame a faint glow of memory, so that every keeper carried the shimmer of past kindnesses.
"If I dim only when unwatched," Doran said, "then my light was only ever a mask.
Why should I blame her hand for the sky's thievery?
"The one who risks the most should not end the night the dimmest," he said.
The keepers asked, "Why match a stranger so exactly?"

note: Doran's own lantern whispers temptations he refuses; glow of memory reputation; turn away only from repeat drinkers.

enough that they would stand richer than if they had never trusted.

quotes.text: I will not punish a whole life of open hands for a single thin tide.
The eel slid onto the stones. "They held something back," it said. "Answer thin with thin."
*Read the long shore, not the single shell. Trust earned in many tides deserves your whole hand.*
In the seventh season of Anwe's pearls
Wherever pearls crossed, a small white shell settled on the bank, and each shell told how its maker had given and returned.
"You will never see this one again," it said. "The ring is wide. Who would know?"
"Such trust deserves more than half."
*Answer the intent, not the fog.
"A debt settled is a door closed," she said.

note: Tavi refuses the eel every season; shells as reputation; Anwe carves a numbered line each season.

quotes.text: "Many dim nights are a choice. Answer choices, not shadow."

quotes.text: In the first season, the western elder grew greedy and kept everything. The next dawn, the baskets stopped.
